This role exists to protect and scale it. As Executive Assistant to the Founders, you'll own the calendars, inboxes, and travel of both the CEO and CTO, and you'll be the person who makes sure the highest-leverage meeting happens on the right day with the right prep in hand. You'll operate with real judgment and real context: you'll know what matters this quarter, who the important clients and candidates are, and what can wait. jobs.description_text: We help governments build infrastructure faster with hardware, software, and AI — turning street-level capture into living intelligence that 500+ cities and towns across the country use to see what's out there, direct the work, and fix problems before they fail. We believe in a future where infrastructure keeps up with society. Every street, sidewalk, bridge … everywhere. jobs.description_text: The Role As a Controls Software Engineer on the Pointing & Tracking team, you will own the software control loop that keeps a laser precisely pointed between two moving platforms, both satellite-to-ground and satellite-to-satellite. jobs.title: Embedded Systems Engineer, Robotics
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE We're looking for an Embedded Systems Engineer to own the boundary where our robot's electronics meet its software. You will bring up and debug new PCBs, write the firmware and drivers that make every sensor, camera, actuator, and compute module talk to each other, and make sure data moves reliably across CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, GMSL, I2C, SPI, and Ethernet. This is a hands-on, cross-layer role. You'll work closely with electrical, firmware, controls, and robotics software engineers, and you'll often be the person who figures out whether a problem lives in hardware, firmware, or software. jobs.title: Open Application - US
jobs.description_text: -- Can't find the right fit but still want to work with us? Apply here -- DRYFT Ideas only change the world when you build them at scale. That’s what Dryft is here for. Dryft builds models that automate complex human decisions in manufacturing operations. We capture the knowledge of experienced operators across supply chain, production planning, engineering and more, simulate the consequences of their decisions, and use this understanding to help run their business. Our customers include some of the largest robotics, machine and component manufacturers in the world. We’re a small, talent-dense team with modest roots and a love for the physical world: cars, machines, planes. Our team includes graduates from Stanford, Berkeley, CDTM and TUM, winners of Stanford TreeHacks, recipients of Fulbright & Haniel scholarships, and people who have built everything from robots and race cars to software with millions of downloads. What matters more to us than credentials is how people work: humility, hard work, speed, kindness, deep customer care, and a willingness to take on problems others avoid. Working at Dryft is hard. You get unusual ownership early on, with real responsibility. But that’s also what makes it one of the biggest learning experiences of your life. We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies. ERPs ran the physical world for half a century.

jobs.title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations [Remote]
jobs.description_text: THE OPPORTUNITY Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. THE ROLE As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. jobs.title: Platform Architect
jobs.description_text: About the Role The company operates 2000+ microservices deployed across dozens of compliance-regulated sites globally. They are transforming this into a modular financial cloud platform — organizing services into 50-100 independently versioned business modules, where each compliance site is a version set (a pinned, validated combination of module versions). As Platform Architect, you will own the version engineering and module governance architecture — the system that ensures every deployment is reproducible, every change's blast radius is computable, and every site composition is a known-good state. This is fundamentally a build systems + dependency management + change propagation problem at financial-grade reliability. Key Responsibilities - Design the version set model: each site defined as a locked, tested combination of module versions (analogous to a Bazel workspace snapshot or Cargo.lock), with version compatibility matrices and automatic constraint solving - Architect reproducible build pipelines: any module at any version produces byte-identical artifacts regardless of when/where it's built; hermetic build environments, content-addressable artifact storage, SLSA Level 3+ provenance - Build and maintain the live dependency graph spanning 2000+ services: static analysis (code/API/schema) + runtime analysis (traffic-weighted call patterns), transitive dependency resolution with automatic conflict detection - Design the monorepo + package ownership governance model: clea

jobs.description_text: Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z. Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you. We crawl the web continuously and cannot keep all of it, refresh all of it, or spend a GPU on all of it. Something has to decide which pages are worth indexing, which links are worth following, which pages say the same thing as pages we already have, what has gone stale, and what we should never have picked up. These decisions are worth more than most ranking work. The cheapest way to improve search is to stop indexing pages nobody should ever retrieve, and to start indexing the ones we are missing. Today they run on a mix of learned signals and thresholds someone picked. We are looking for a research engineer to own the signals behind those decisions, and the decisions themselves. jobs.title: Junior Engineer - Working Student Thesis
jobs.description_text: About the Role: A suspicious web redirect is often just one step in a much larger chain. A traffic distribution system (TDS) decides where a visitor goes next based on signals such as their browser, location, referrer, or previous activity. In malicious campaigns, this can make the infrastructure difficult to observe and the final destination difficult to reach consistently. In this student position, you will investigate TDS infrastructure, understand its routing logic, and develop tools to capture browser activity, reconstruct redirection chains, and map the relationships between their components. The aim is to build a reusable approach to understanding how different TDS instances route visitors from an entry point to a final destination. The work will form the basis of your diploma thesis at Gen. With guidance from the team, you will develop your malware analysis and reverse engineering skills while using AI to help build and validate tooling for TDS research. Key Responsibilities: - Analyze TDS infrastructure and investigate how it routes malicious traffic - Reverse engineer and deobfuscate JavaScript to understand routing and evasion techniques - Inspect and modify HTTP traffic, including headers, cookies, and redirects, using Chrome DevTools, Fiddler, Burp Suite, or similar tools - Use AI to help develop and validate tools in JavaScript, Python, or other scripting languages for automated analysis and infrastructure mapping - Test your findings and document the methods an
